statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). CME equity futures completed their weekly settlement at 21:00Z on Friday and the next reopen is Sunday 22:00Z, so every hour of the published window covers a halted market in which no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop.
recommendation: Tail sits at a weekend floor and no danger window is published, because the forecast horizon contains no U.S. cash session, no CME futures session and no scheduled U.S. macro release. The scores describe deferred gap and headline risk rather than observable intraday structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection rules are unaffected by this assessment. The first genuine repricing checkpoint is the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, which lies exactly at the end of the horizon plus 24 hours; the first scheduled U.S. macro checkpoint is the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index on Monday, followed by the ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS cluster on Tuesday and August payrolls on Friday 4 September.
headline: Weekend halt holds after a hawkish Jackson Hole Friday: NQ settled at 29,509.50 with equity volatility contained
body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address on Friday reset September policy expectations, with market-implied odds of a rate increase rising to roughly 60% from about 35% beforehand on CME futures pricing. The repricing was expressed mainly in rates: the 2-year Treasury yield rose about 11 basis points to 4.34%, its highest in a month, the 10-year added roughly 5 basis points to 4.72%, and the 30-year finished near 5.21%, a policy-led flattening rather than a term-premium shock. Equity damage stayed contained and internally split. Cash NDX closed at 29,433.43 (-0.70%) within a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range and NQ futures settled the week at 29,509.50 (-0.63%), both in the lower part of their session ranges, but the decline was rotational: semiconductors gave back part of the Nvidia-led advance while other large index members held up better and the Dow finished near unchanged. VIX eased to 14.43 in a 14.13-14.84 range, so implied volatility did not confirm a stress event. Energy remained a stabilising input, with WTI near $83.44 after a weekly decline of about 4% and Brent near $89.31, down more than 5% on the week, as Gulf export flows improved even though the Strait of Hormuz stayed operationally unstable. Because CME equity futures settled at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, the entire 24-hour publication window covers a halted market. The pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures cannot form without an open venue, so Tail is held at a floor while Stress carries the deferred weekend gap and headline risk, principally an unresolved Hormuz situation and a policy debate that has shifted toward the possibility of an increase. Shared Finviz cross-asset context for this run was collected at 19:37Z, outside the 90-minute freshness bound, and was therefore treated as stale and excluded from the evidence base; the assessment rests on verified Friday closing data, primary yield and oil sources, and verified reporting.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 hours span the quiet overnight stretch before the Jackson Hole address, the repricing itself and the weekly settlement. Overnight Asian and European hours held Tail near 11-12 with Stress around 49-55 and a mixed mode. Tail and Stress lifted through the U.S. morning as the speech reset September rate expectations, peaking at Tail 22 and Stress 64 in the 17:00Z hour with an event/whipsaw mode while short yields rose and gold fell. Price discovery stayed orderly: retracements occurred, VIX eased rather than spiked and the decline was rotational rather than broad, so Tail never approached the block threshold. After the 20:00Z cash close and the 21:00Z futures settlement, Tail and Stress collapsed to weekend levels of 7-8 and 26-30 with a normal mode. One slot, the 10:00Z hour, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published window runs from the current hour through Saturday 22:00Z and contains no cash session, no CME futures session and no scheduled U.S. release; the Sunday 22:00Z reopen sits exactly 24 hours beyond the final slot. With no venue open, the pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures cannot form, so Tail is held at a 6-7 floor throughout and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window. Stress decays from 25 to a weekend low of 20 through the European Saturday hours before rebuilding to 25 by the end of the window as the interval of unpriced weekend information widens ahead of the reopen. Confidence declines gradually from 84 to 78, which is an ageing adjustment rather than a sign of conflicting sources: Friday's closing data, yields, oil and volatility are verified and internally consistent, but the newest market observation keeps growing older with no tick able to replace it. The genuine risk carried across this window is a single reopen gap plus weekend headline flow, principally the unresolved Strait of Hormuz situation and any further policy commentary on the closing day of the symposium. A gap alone is not the repeated extension after failed retracements that Tail measures, so a Tail revision would require observed post-reopen structure rather than the size of the opening print.
